title: Gemma 3 Technical Report
data_curation: Pre-training uses token budgets of 14T (27B), 12T (12B), 4T (4B), and 2T (1B), mixing text and images, with more multilingual data (monolingual and parallel) balanced via a Unimax-inspired sampling strategy (Chung et al.). The tokenizer is Gemini 2.0's SentencePiece (262k vocab). Filtering removes unsafe utterances, PII, and sensitive data; eval sets are decontaminated; quality reweighing follows Sachdeva et al. Distillation samples 256 logits per token weighted by teacher probabilities. Vision data: each image maps to 256 soft tokens from a frozen 400M SigLIP encoder at 896x896, with Pan & Scan adaptive windowing at inference. Post-training data filters out PII, toxic outputs, mistaken self-identification, and duplicates, while adding subsets that encourage in-context attribution, hedging, and refusals. Reward signals come from weight-averaged reward models on human feedback, code execution feedback (Rlef), and ground-truth math rewards (DeepSeek-R1, Tulu 3).
curriculum: Training proceeds pre-train (with distillation) -> long-context extension -> instruction tuning (distillation + RL) -> optional QAT. Pre-training starts at 32K sequences, then 4B/12B/27B are scaled to 128K at the end of pre-training via RoPE rescaling (factor 8), with the global-attention RoPE base raised from 10k to 1M while local layers stay at 10k. Instruction tuning combines knowledge distillation from a large IT teacher with an RL fine-tuning phase built on improved BOND, WARM, and WARP; reward functions target helpfulness, math, coding, reasoning, instruction-following, and multilinguality while minimizing harmfulness. SFT and RLHF are also used for safety alignment. Finally, Quantization Aware Training (~5,000 steps) produces per-channel int4, per-block int4, and switched-fp8 checkpoints from the non-quantized models.
method: The core post-training contribution is a combined distillation + RL recipe. Distillation from a large IT teacher uses on-policy distillation ideas (Agarwal et al.), sampling 256 teacher logits per token for a cross-entropy target. The RL phase integrates improved BOND (best-of-n distillation alignment), WARM (weight-averaged reward models for reward stability), and WARP (weight-averaged rewarded policies). Rewards span human-feedback reward models, code execution feedback (Rlef, Gehring et al.), and verifiable ground-truth math rewards (DeepSeek-R1, Tulu 3). Architecturally, Gemma 3 swaps Gemma 2's soft-capping for QK-norm and uses a 5:1 local:global attention interleave with a 1024-token sliding window to curb KV-cache growth at 128K context. A frozen SigLIP vision encoder plus Pan & Scan provides multimodality. The problem solved is a lightweight, long-context, multimodal open model competitive with far larger systems.
eval_metrics: Evaluated on LMSYS Chatbot Arena (blind Elo), MMLU/MMLU-Pro, AGIEval, MATH, GSM8K, HiddenMath, GPQA Diamond, MBPP/HumanEval (pass@1), LiveCodeBench, Bird-SQL, SimpleQA, FACTS Grounding, IFEval, BBH, BBEH, N2C, Global-MMLU-Lite, MGSM, WMT24++, FLoRes, XQuAD, ECLeKTic, IndicGenBench; vision: MMMU, DocVQA, InfoVQA, TextVQA, AI2D, ChartQA, VQAv2, MathVista; long-context: RULER and MRCR at 32K/128K; plus memorization-rate and CBRN safety audits. Headline: Gemma-3-27B-IT reaches Chatbot Arena Elo 1338 (rank ~9, above DeepSeek-V3 at 1318 and Gemma 2 at 1220), MATH 89.0, GSM8K 95.9, HumanEval 87.8, MMLU-Pro 67.5, IFEval 90.4, comparable to Gemini-1.5-Pro; Gemma3-4B-IT rivals Gemma2-27B-IT.
key_results: Gemma-3-27B-IT scores Chatbot Arena Elo 1338 (rank ~9), MATH 89.0, GSM8K 95.9, HumanEval 87.8, MMLU-Pro 67.5, and IFEval 90.4, comparable to Gemini-1.5-Pro and ahead of larger open models like DeepSeek-V3 (1318) and Gemma 2 (1220). Gemma3-4B-IT is competitive with Gemma2-27B-IT.
evolution_note: Building on Gemma 2's distillation-based pre-training, Gemma 3 (2025) folds in the 2024 RL-alignment toolkit (BOND/WARM/WARP) and verifiable-reward signals popularized by DeepSeek-R1 and Tulu 3, packaging distillation-plus-RL post-training into lightweight multimodal open models. It anticipates later 2025 work on efficient long-context multimodal open models and on-policy distillation.
